title: Patches, contrastive pairs, tagging losses, and average precision
brief: Count and cut AST's spectrogram patches, write CLAP's symmetric contrastive loss and a zero-shot classifier, and score multi-label tagging with a stable sigmoid cross-entropy and mean average precision.
hints: ast_patch_grid is the output-size formula of a strided convolution: (size - patch) // stride + 1 along each axis.
patchify: build a (n_f, n_t, patch, patch) grid of row indices and one of column indices with broadcasting, index the spectrogram once, then reshape.
multilabel_bce: the stable form of -[y log s(x) + (1 - y) log(1 - s(x))] is max(x, 0) - x * y + log1p(exp(-|x|)). Average over every clip and every class.
average_precision: sort the labels by descending score, take the cumulative count of positives divided by the rank, and average that precision only at the ranks where the label is 1.
mean_average_precision: call average_precision on each column and average, skipping any class that has no positive clip, because its precision is undefined.
clap_loss: after F.normalize, the logits are a @ t.T / tau; F.cross_entropy(logits, arange(N)) is the audio-to-text half and F.cross_entropy(logits.T, arange(N)) the text-to-audio half.

zero_shot_classify: normalize both the clip embeddings and the prompt embeddings to unit length before the matrix product, then take argmax over the class axis. A prompt with a long embedding wins every dot product otherwise.
